name: TechHive

sources.title: TechHive homepage — live Foundry (ex-IDG) consumer-tech publication; categories include Personal Software, Smart Home, Cord-Cutter Confidential; footer has Contact Us and Advertise links

requirements: Not a directory — earned editorial only; staff-written reviews, deals, how-tos, and 'Smart Answers' Q&A
Pitches go through the Contact Us page (techhive.com/about — 'Contact Us' footer link)
Consumer-tech remit: smart home, streaming/cord-cutting, personal software, Windows, security/privacy products
Physical review products historically mattered more than SaaS — a consumer-software angle is the realistic pitch
Foundry also runs 'BrandPosts' — clearly-labeled client content via the Advertise link (paid)
preparation: A consumer-facing angle: smart home device/service, streaming tool, personal software, privacy/security app
Pitch via the Contact Us page; brand-content inquiries via the Advertise link
workflow: Open the footer 'Contact Us' page and pitch the relevant editor/desk
For reviews, expect to supply review access; for deals coverage, a live consumer deal
Paid alternative: Foundry 'BrandPosts' client-content program via Advertise
Coverage, if it happens, is a staff-written article or inclusion in a roundup
watchFor: Smart-home/streaming heritage — pure B2B SaaS is off-beat
BrandPosts are paid labeled content, not earned coverage — don't conflate the two
Part of Foundry (formerly IDG) — same editorial family as PCWorld/Macworld/Tech Advisor; a pitch can be routed across sibling sites
countsAsLive: A TechHive article, review, or roundup entry mentioning the product is published at techhive.com
unknowns: Editor-by-editor contact details — the contact page wasn't fully captured this session
Review-unit policies for software vs hardware
